title: Sentinel logging TF module: cross-account CloudTrail + OpenSearch ILM + retention guardrails
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (sentinel-logging) that provisions cross-account CloudTrail ingestion, S3 archival with lifecycle to Glacier/Deep Archive, an OpenSearch index lifecycle management (ILM) policy, and alerting/health checks. The module should be pluggable into private (VPC) deployments and compatible with both Redwood Private and Dedicated edge cases. Focus: retention guardrails, KMS-encrypted buckets, index rollover, and safe upgrade path for ILM changes.
acceptance_criteria: Module can be consumed by a Private deployment stack and provisions CloudTrail with cross-account role and S3 sink
S3 bucket is encrypted with customer or platform KMS and enforces block public access
OpenSearch ILM policy created with hot-warm-cold phases and explicit rollover/forcemerge settings
Automated retention enforcement (S3 lifecycle + OpenSearch ILM) applied and verifiable via healthcheck
Healthcheck Lambda (or container) returns OK/Degraded with metrics exported to console (index age, S3 size, missing snapshots)
Upgrade path documented: ILM policy changes are applied safely without data loss using blue/green ILM rollout steps
Integration tests validate cross-account role assumption, KMS permissions, and ILM transitions
At least one GitHub PR with CI passing (Terraform validate/plan) and a security review ticket linked
implementation_steps: Define module inputs: account IDs, KMS key ARN, opensearch domain endpoint, log-prefix, retention_days, ilm_policy_json_path
Implement cloudtrail.tf: create organization-trail or single-account trail with sns/sqs forwarding option and s3 bucket sink
Implement s3.tf: create bucket with server-side-encryption (kms), lifecycle rules to transition to Glacier/Deep Archive and eventual expiration
Implement iam.tf: cross-account role/policy for CloudTrail to write to bucket and for ingestion lambda to read
Implement opensearch.tf: index template, ILM policy, and initial alias/rollover config compatible with existing indices
Write healthchecks.tf: Lambda/function container that checks index age, ILM step, recent S3 write events, and writes metrics to CloudWatch/Console
Add tests: terratest and unit tests for templates, smoke deploy in staging, and policy simulation for KMS/iam
Add upgrade playbook in docs directory describing safe ILM transitions and rollback steps
test_plan: Unit: terraform fmt/validate on module and example usage
Integration: deploy example into staging account using a CI job; verify CloudTrail events are delivered for 24h
Chaos: simulate missing permissions (remove kms:Encrypt) and ensure module failure is explicit with remediation hints
ILM migration test: create old ILM policy, deploy new module, run migration script and verify no index loss
Load test: synthetic event stream to validate OpenSearch indexing and ILM trigger for rollover
notes: Trade-offs: We chose ILM policy templating over hard-coded values to allow customers to tune hot/warm thresholds per workload. This increases complexity but avoids one-size-fits-all corner cases.
Decision: Use S3 lifecycle for cold storage + OpenSearch snapshots for recoverability. Snapshots require additional snapshot repository (S3 + role) - documented in the module examples.
Ops concern: Changing an ILM policy in-place can cause immediate index merges; provide a blue/green ILM rollout script that creates new index template + alias switch.
Security: KMS key rotation and grant scoping must be validated by a security reviewer. We will supply a policy generator for least-privilege grants.
Compatibility: Module supports both Elasticsearch-compatible OpenSearch 1.x domains and managed AWS OpenSearch endpoints. Tests will include both variants.
Fallback: If OpenSearch is not available, module can be configured to use S3-only archival and notify via SNS; this is for air-gapped/private installs where a separate analytics cluster is offloaded.
